what: Road surface of the existing situation: the ground between the survey's own road lines (DWG layers YOL_SOSE, YOL_TOPRAK, YOL_BORDUR, YOL_KOPRU as cached by the Basemap script). Rings in survey m, to be painted together even-odd (holes included). A fill only: its edge is not a surveyed line and is never drawn as one; the survey's lines are drawn on top.
method: Along the town's streets (OpenStreetMap bands, used only to say where a street is): the ground reached from the street's centre line without crossing a survey road line, a building line or a wall, through no opening under 3 m, kept only where a survey road line lies within 14 m on both opposite sides (8 directions) with no building line in between.
Without a street of the street file (tracks, bank roads): the ground between two survey road edge lines up to 9 m apart, stretches of 25 m or more.
Seams of 1 m closed, parts under 30 m2 dropped, outline simplified to 0.35 m. Raster cell 0.5 m, so the surface follows a survey line to about 0.5 m.
Checked by eye against Esri World Imagery (Maxar, 1 Mar 2023) on the whole frame at 2.5 to 3 px per m.
limits: Where the survey draws only one edge of a road, or none (old town streets between house fronts), there is no surface. At a street mouth or a break in a survey line the surface's own edge is an estimate (fill edge only). A few forecourts and the wedge between two converging tracks are filled where survey road lines enclose them.
